# ataila_project_backup_sets (Data Source)

A project's backup sets, newest first: what each run copied of one environment. A project keeps many sets, so a read keeps at most `limit` (100 when left out); `more` says whether further sets matched. Where a set is stored and its manifest stay in the portal.

Needs `project-backup-read-global` (or the admin key); a tenant-scoped token reads its own tenant's projects. Platform release 1.0.399 or later.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# The newest successful PROD sets of a project.
data "ataila_project_backup_sets" "prod" {
  project_id  = ataila_project.shop.id
  environment = "prod"
  status      = "success"
  limit       = 10
}

output "last_prod_backup" {
  value = try(data.ataila_project_backup_sets.prod.sets[0].finished_at, null)
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `project_id` (String) Id of the project.

### Optional

- `environment` (String) Only this environment's sets: `dev`, `uat` or `prod`.
- `limit` (Number) The most sets to keep, newest first: 1-1000; 100 when left out.
- `status` (String) Only the sets in this status: `queued`, `running`, `success`, `failed` or `pruned`.
- `tier` (String) Only the sets of this tier: `daily`, `weekly`, `monthly`, `yearly` or `manual` (Back up now).

### Read-Only

- `more` (Boolean) True when more sets matched than `limit` kept.
- `sets` (Attributes List) The matching sets, newest first. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--sets))

<a id="nestedatt--sets"></a>
### Nested Schema for `sets`

Read-Only:

- `attempt` (Number) The run's attempt number: above 1 after a retry.
- `bytes` (Number) The set's size in bytes, once it finished.
- `components` (List of String) What it carries: `code`, `database`, `files`.
- `created_at` (String) When the set was requested (RFC 3339, UTC).
- `environment` (String) `dev`, `uat` or `prod`.
- `error` (String) Why it failed, as the run reported it.
- `finished_at` (String) When its run finished.
- `has_checksums` (Boolean) True when the set was completed with its checksum list, written last: a set without one is not complete.
- `id` (String) The set's id.
- `pruned_at` (String) When retention removed it.
- `started_at` (String) When its run started.
- `status` (String) `queued`, `running`, `success`, `failed`, or `pruned` (a success removed by retention).
- `tier` (String) The tier that made it, or `manual`.
